Containerlab Verification Report

BIND9 Anycast DNS Testbed

A 10-node containerized testbed demonstrating BGP Anycast with ECMP multipath distribution across recursive caching resolvers and authoritative secondaries. Features split-horizon views, automated AXFR zone replication, forwarder loops, and absolute RFC 6761 internet isolation.

Plane 01 — Topology

Topology

Ten containers on one router. isp-r1 (AS 65000) runs FRR with maximum-paths 2 and bgp bestpath as-path multipath-relax, so both anycast /32s are ECMP-installed, not primary/backup. Three broadcast segments hang off its data interfaces over host bridges; the management plane (10.233.4.0/24) rides a separate VRF and never enters BGP. Hover a node for its details; click it to jump to its configuration.

Forwarding variant
isp-r1
Core router (AS 65000)
Management IP 10.233.4.11
Data IPs 172.21.21.254 · 172.22.22.1 · 172.23.23.1 · 172.25.25.1 · 172.26.26.1
Anycast VIP none (announces neither /32)
FRR / BIND FRR 8.5.2 (bgpd + zebra) · no BIND
DNS role BGP core, ECMP to both anycast planes

Plane 03 — Resolution path

How a Query Actually Travels

A query for www.lab.test from pc crosses the cache anycast, the recursive tier, the lab root, and the authoritative anycast before the answer returns. The hop-by-hop proof is dig +trace, shown verbatim beside the path. The animated version of this same path is the play control in the topology section.

Seven hops, variant normal
01
pc → 172.31.31.81 (cache anycast)
resolv.conf nameserver; ECMP sends the query to bc-cache1 or bc-cache2 (id.server flips between them)
02
cache → bc-rmaster 172.23.23.97 (recursive view)
cache view is forward only to 172.23.23.97 / .129 / .100; rmaster’s recursive view accepts it
03
bc-rmaster → lab root 172.26.26.53
rmaster recurses; its hints file contains exactly one address, ns.root. 172.26.26.53 — the lab root, never a real root
04
root answers: lab.test NS = ns100.lab.test, 172.30.30.85
root zone test. delegates lab.test. to the authoritative anycast address
05
rmaster → 172.30.30.85 (authoritative anycast)
served by bc-rslave1 or bc-rslave2; both AXFR’d lab.test from rmaster, serial 2026081501
06
answer returns: slave → rmaster → cache
each resolver caches; the answer rides the same path back
07
cache → pc: NOERROR, www.lab.test = 10.10.10.10
client sees a normal positive answer, id 44417 in the evidence below
dig +trace www.lab.test (from pc) 
$ docker exec clab-dns-pc dig +trace www.lab.test
;; Received 76 bytes from 172.31.31.81#53(172.31.31.81) in 2 ms
lab.test.  86400  IN  NS  ns100.lab.test.
;; Received 105 bytes from 172.26.26.53#53(ns.root) in 0 ms
www.lab.test.  86400  IN  A  10.10.10.10
;; Received 121 bytes from 172.30.30.85#53(ns100.lab.test) in 0 ms
pc resolv.conf · plain dig 
$ docker exec clab-dns-pc cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 172.31.31.81

$ docker exec clab-dns-pc dig www.lab.test
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 44417
www.lab.test.  86285  IN  A  10.10.10.10
;; SERVER: 172.31.31.81#53(172.31.31.81) (UDP)
No real root server is ever contacted
The trace shows three responders and only three: the cache anycast (76 bytes), the lab root ns.root (105 bytes), and the authoritative anycast (121 bytes). The lab root serves ., test. and arpa. itself, so resolution never leaves the 172.16.0.0/12 lab space.
Plane 04 — Failure, on purpose

Forwarding Variants

The lab deploys the resolver chain in two variants, switched by ./dns-deploy.sh. normal is the working configuration; loop is deliberately broken — it points the cache’s forwarders at ex-dns, which forwards straight back, and the query circles until BIND times out and answers SERVFAIL. Switch the toggle; the stanzas and results below follow.

normal · cache → recursive tier NOERROR · 10.10.10.10

bc-cache1 / bc-cache2 named.conf, view “cache” — forward to the two recursive tiers on 172.23.23.0/24:

view "cache" {
    match-clients { 172.21.21.1; };
    recursion yes;

    forwarders { 172.23.23.97; 172.23.23.129; 172.23.23.100; };
    forward only;

bc-rmaster “recursive” view — strict ACL, exactly the two cache addresses:

view "recursive" {
    match-clients { 172.22.22.100; 172.22.22.200; };
dig www.lab.test from pc — works 
$ docker exec clab-dns-pc dig www.lab.test
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 44417
www.lab.test.  86285  IN  A  10.10.10.10
;; SERVER: 172.31.31.81#53(172.31.31.81) (UDP)
loop · the circle SERVFAIL after timeout

The cache now forwards to ex-dns first — and ex-dns forwards back to the recursive tier and the root, so the same query arrives at rmaster from rmaster’s own address (see the log below). 

view "cache" {
    match-clients { 172.21.21.1; };
    recursion yes;

    forwarders { 172.25.25.127; 172.23.23.97; 172.23.23.129; };
    forward only;

bc-rmaster “recursive” view — same circular forwarders, widened ACL so the loop can form:

view "recursive" {
    match-clients { 172.22.22.0/24; 172.23.23.0/24; 172.25.25.0/24; };

    forwarders { 172.25.25.127; 172.23.23.97; 172.23.23.129; };
    forward only;

ex-dns also points back at the recursive tier and the root — closing the cycle:

options {
    forwarders { 172.23.23.97; 172.23.23.129; 172.26.26.53; };
    forward only;
dig www.lab.test from pc — SERVFAIL 
$ docker exec clab-dns-pc dig www.lab.test
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1

Live confirmation that the loop stanza is what is actually deployed: docker exec clab-dns-bc-cache1 grep -A1 forwarders /etc/bind/named.conf → forwarders { 172.25.25.127; 172.23.23.97; 172.23.23.129; }; / forward only;

ex-dns log — the same query arriving, repeatedly, from three different servers 
18:31:56.690 client 172.23.23.97#48140  (www.lab.test): query: www.lab.test IN A
18:31:56.690 client 172.22.22.200#36763 (www.lab.test): query: www.lab.test IN A
18:31:59.093 client 172.23.23.129#34730 (www.lab.test): query: www.lab.test IN A
18:32:00.294 client 172.23.23.97#36009  (www.lab.test): query: www.lab.test IN A
18:32:02.697 client 172.23.23.129#45295 (www.lab.test): query: www.lab.test IN A
bc-rmaster log — note the first line: rmaster is receiving its own query, from its own address 172.23.23.97 
18:32:04.285 client 172.23.23.97#42653  view recursive: query failed (timed out)
18:32:04.285 client 172.25.25.127#47049 view recursive: query failed (timed out)
18:32:04.285 client 172.22.22.200#59949 view recursive: query failed (timed out)
18:32:04.298 client 172.25.25.127#37659 view recursive: query failed (SERVFAIL)
The widened ACL is deliberate — and it is the one departure from the literal spec

An earlier prediction said the loop would fail immediately with REFUSED, because 172.23.23.97 is not inside the recursive view’s strict match-clients. In practice that was wrong: dns-deploy.sh widens match-clients in the loop variant to { 172.22.22.0/24; 172.23.23.0/24; 172.25.25.0/24; }, so the self-query does match the recursive view and times out instead of being refused. In normal the ACL stays strict, as specified.

That widening is a deliberate and correct choice — with the strict ACL the loop would never form, because every hop would be REFUSED immediately and there would be nothing to observe. It is the one place the loop variant departs from the literal original spec.

Plane 09 — Where everything lives

Architecture & Origin

Where the source of truth lives, how the lab is deployed, and how this report was produced.

Source of truth

~/Github/bind9-lab/anycast-dns/ on the laptop — full git history; every rendered config is checked in, including both variants of named.conf.

Live deployment

~/lab/dns on clab-mini — where containerlab and the VS Code containerlab extension expect labs to live on that host. The lab name is dns; containers are clab-dns-<node>.

Host bridges

Three Linux bridges interconnect the routing interfaces: br-dnscache (172.22.22.0/24), br-dnsrec (172.23.23.0/24), br-dnsext (172.26.26.0/24 & 172.25.25.0/24). Created by setup.sh, removed by teardown.sh.

Why the lab is sealed

RFC 6761 reserves .test for testing — it can never appear in the real root zone. Combined with a fake root (172.26.26.53) whose hints file contains exactly one address, resolution physically cannot leave the lab. www.google.com answers NXDOMAIN as proof.

Deploy workflow

  • ./setup.sh — create host bridges
  • ./deploy.sh normal — containerlab up, VRFs, static data routes
  • ./dns-deploy.sh <variant> — render, push, validate, reload
  • ./validate.sh — 15-check functional suite

How this report was built

Every output quoted here was captured against the live lab on clab-mini and read back verbatim; the lab was left in the normal variant, unchanged. Commands and outputs are exact. Generated 2026-08-15.

Two planes, one meaning
Teal marks the recursive plane — anything clients query (the cache anycast). Ochre marks the authoritative plane — anything that owns zones (the slave anycast). The two anycast services are 172.31.31.81/32 and 172.30.30.85/32, both ECMP across two members each; the management plane (10.233.4.0/24) never enters BGP.
